guidance: Separate permissibility from feasibility. An action's checks say only whether the actor is allowed or positioned to begin it (rules of the game, location, possession). Never check whether the attempt will succeed: do not refuse an action because a resource is too low to finish it. Starting a multi-step activity sets the actor's or object's activity state. Autonomous processes then advance that activity every tick, consume or produce stocks, and switch the activity to a stopped or failed state when a needed stock runs out, or to a finished state when it completes. Every numeric stock needs a process or action for each way it can rise and each way it can fall.

assumptions: The partnership contains exactly four countries and one regional health network.
The four countries are represented as a 100-by-100 regional coordinate grid; coordinates and the 100-unit regional extent are estimated because no geography is specified.
The decision deadline is estimated as 26 weeks after simulation start.
Regular meetings occur once per week and last 4 hours; both values are estimates.
Each group uses a distinct communication channel, and each new concern is routed to one randomly selected recipient member.
All generated concerns are true but local, as stated in the scenario.
Concern generation rates are estimated at 0.4 per week for technical, 0.3 per week for legal, 0.3 per week for logistics, and 0.5 per week for community groups.
Initial country support is estimated at 60 points out of 100, and activation requires at least 50 points from every country.
One unresolved concern reduces the recipient country's support by 1 point; this effect size is an estimated simplification.
One unresolved concern consumes 1 meeting hour, and every 3 unresolved concerns reopens one settled issue; these rates are estimated simplifications.
Activation requires approval from all four countries; unanimity is an estimated rule-of-the-game simplification.
Initial technical capacity of 70 percent, legal clearance of 50 percent, logistics capacity of 60 percent, and community acceptance of 50 percent are estimated baseline values.
The threshold values for activation are set equal to those initial readiness values because the scenario gives no explicit thresholds.

Deployment progress increases by 5 percentage points per week after activation, and delay reduces progress by 2 percentage points per week when unresolved concerns exceed 8; both rates and the threshold are estimated.
Technical, logistics, and community capacities decline by 1 percentage point per operating week after activation; this depletion rate is estimated.
The system's operational lifetime is estimated as 520 weeks.
A concern has severity of 1 point by default because the scenario says concerns are small; severity variation is omitted.
The model treats support, readiness, acceptance, and capacity as bounded from 0 to 100.
Private concerns remain unobservable to actors outside their originating channel until formally routed or discussed.
No physical travel, monetary budget, disease transmission, or surveillance detections are modeled because the scenario does not specify them.
A system failure occurs when any required readiness capacity reaches 0 percent after activation.
The simulation stops activation after the deadline, while an already active system may continue operating until failure or expiration.
processes_each_tick: Reduce the decision deadline's time remaining by 1 week.
Each concern group generates a stochastic number of true local concerns with mean equal to its concern generation rate.
Route each new concern through its group's separate channel to one randomly selected country or network member.
Increase the recipient's received and unresolved concern counts when concerns arrive.
Decrease each country's decision support by 1 point for each newly received unresolved concern, with a floor of 0.
Hold one regular partnership meeting and consume meeting time on active concerns.
Use 1 meeting hour per unresolved concern considered, up to the meeting's 4-hour duration.
Reopen one previously settled issue for every 3 unresolved concerns considered, with a minimum of zero reopened issues.
Reduce available meeting time by 0.5 hours for each reopened issue, with a floor of zero.
Reduce deployment progress by 2 percentage points for every week in which unresolved concerns exceed 8, with a floor of zero.
Increase deployment progress by 5 percentage points per week after activation when all required capacities and approvals remain sufficient, with a ceiling of 100.
Reduce technical, legal, logistics, and community capacity by 1 percentage point per week after activation to represent routine resource depletion.
If any required capacity reaches 0 percent after activation, change system status to failed.
If the deadline reaches 0 weeks while the system is inactive, record the decision as missed and stop further activation attempts.
If the system operates for its 520-week lifetime, change its status to expired.

scenario_text: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.
